text.p: Bonds were gaining slightly in line with the the firmer international trend with the spread between the benchmark 10-year cash and the Bunds consolidating around 90 basis points.

But the greatest potential for gains was seen at the shorter end where investors were likely to be encouraged by expectations of a rate cut soon -- possibly on Friday -- by the Bank of Portugal and the firm escudo.
The spread with the 10-year Bund stood at 89 basis points, unchanged on Tuesday's close.
"A cut of 25 basis points by the Bank of Portugal is not totally discounted in prices at the short end. Therefore, gains are almost certain," said one trader.

The spread between the March 1999 OT (Portuguese bond) and the February 2007 OT was unchanged at 97 basis points. "The spread between the two and the 10 years has to rise above 100 and perhaps even reach 110 basis points," said one trader.
The escudo was steady at 100.32/34 to the mark against its 100.31/34 opening.
